title: Gateway Check
subtitle: Domestic abuse evidence for legal aid, checked before it is submitted. Ministry of Justice · 10DS hackathon, 6 October 2026

slides.heading: The solicitor sees what is missing and what to ask for
slides.caption: Letter checked against Schedule 1 in about 20 seconds: 7 of 8 requirements met, the one gap named, the request to the author already drafted.

slides.heading: The corrected letter shows what it fixed, on the letter itself
slides.caption: Missing → Included, with the new sentence quoted. Every mark is a sentence found word for word in the PDF.

slides.heading: The client uploads from their phone and gets a plain answer
slides.caption: One-off link, camera or file. No legal wording, no "rejected": ready, needs a change, or your solicitor will look at it.

slides.heading: The caseworker gets the evidence, an independent re-check and the look-ups
slides.caption: Queue sorted by verdict. Each review: marks on the letter, party check, email domain and offence list verified. The decision stays with the person.

slides.heading: One case, three people, live
slides.caption: Client phone, solicitor and caseworker side by side on the same case.

closing.heading: Does it work?
lines: MoJ's own example letters: 24 of 24 as PDFs, 11 of 12 as text
146 synthetic cases across all 22 paragraphs: 146 of 146
No false approvals. Anything unclear goes to a person.
Every result rests on a quote found word for word; three checks must agree; names are matched in code.
